subject: Post-demo: Performance / SLO checklist & next steps \u0004 AcmePay
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@acmepay.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Performance / SLO checklist & next steps - AcmePay

Hi John / Priya,

Thanks again for your time on today	s demo - really appreciate the clear signal on the use case and traffic patterns. Per our conversation Im attaching a short SLO checklist to capture the performance constraints we'll validate before an evaluation/POC decision. Key items we call out:

- Latency target (p95): your target vs. current baseline
- Throughput: average qps and expected daily/weekly throughput
- Concurrency: expected simultaneous sessions (burst vs. steady)
- Streaming / partial-response requirements (if any)
- Error budgets and acceptable failure modes

Attached: acmepay-slo-checklist.xlsx (simple checklist + fields for you to fill). I also attached a short PDF recap of the demo and sample perf numbers from a comparable customer using the same model family.

Next steps I propose:
1) You fill the checklist (or confirm below) - where possible include a short sample dataset or representative payloads.
2) We'll schedule a short performance validation run with our SEs (30-60 min) to run against a test harness (we'll provide metrics & logs). Rishi / Dev, can you make time this week?
3) We'll share a decision-criteria summary (latency, cost per 1M tokens, ability to stream) so you have a concrete rubric.

John - could you confirm the p95 latency target you want us to validate and whether streaming partial responses is required for your product? That will determine the configuration we'll run.

Thanks,

- Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: acmepay-slo-checklist.xlsx
Attachment: redwood-performance-run-0502.pdf

From: John Miller <john.miller@acmepay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO checklist & next steps - AcmePay

Marissa - thanks for the follow-up and the checklist. Quick answers below so we can move to the perf run: 

- p95 latency target: 80ms end-to-end for the user-facing text generation call (we can accept up to 100ms as a stretch, but 80ms is the desired bar).
- Throughput: baseline ~10k requests/day; expected growth to ~50k requests/day within 3-6 months of launch.
- Concurrency: typical steady-state 40-60 concurrent sessions, peak bursts up to 300 for marketing-driven spikes.
- Streaming: yes - streaming partial responses is required for our UX (progressive rendering).
- Error budget: we target <0.5% errors per day; anything above 1% would trigger escalation.

We can attach a small representative payload set (100 requests) and a link to a anonymized sample dataset. I'll ask Priya to drop that in the Drive folder.

Can you confirm what GPU type / instance you plan to use for the validation run and whether we should expect any model quantization that would materially change output quality? Also please confirm the metrics you will report (p50/p95, throughput, token cost, memory usage, stream latency).

- John Miller | Director, Platform Engineering
AcmePay
john.miller@acmepay.com | +1 646-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@acmepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO checklist & next steps - AcmePay

Thanks John - this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Looping in Rishi (SE) and Dev (Solutions) to coordinate the validation run.

Rishi / Dev: AcmePay is asking for a perf validation that covers: p95 <= 80ms target (stretch 100ms), streaming enabled, concurrency bursts up to 300, baseline throughput target ~50k/day. They will provide 100 representative payloads and a small sample dataset in the Drive link (Priya, thanks in advance). Please confirm:

- Preferred run window (Rishi/Dev): this week or early next week - we should aim for a 45-60 minute slot.
- Runtime config: model variant suggestion, GPU type (we typically run initial validations on A100/RTX8000 equivalent), quantization profile (we'll avoid heavy quantization for the first run to preserve output quality), and expected tokenization behavior.
- Deliverables: perf summary (p50/p95, throughput, token costs), streaming latency (time-to-first-byte for partial responses), memory/CPU utilization, and logs for debugging.

I'll also add a short decision-criteria checklist to the Drive folder so John/Priya can review.

Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, John Miller <john.miller@acmepay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO checklist & next steps - AcmePay

Thanks for the context - happy to run this. Proposed plan:

1) Test harness: we'll use our isolated perf harness (link: https://app.redwood.ai/run/performancerun-0502) with streaming enabled to measure time-to-first-byte and tail latencies.
2) Hardware: we'll allocate an A100-class instance for the initial run (no aggressive quantization) to mirror expected production SLOs. If you want a cost-optimized run we can show a follow-up with an INT8-like quantized variant.
3) Data & keys: Priya, please drop the 100-sample payloads (anonymized) in the Drive folder and, if possible, a short CSV mapping of request types to expected token counts. We'll need a temporary test API key from your side (or we can provide an ephemeral key) so we can route runs to the harness.
4) Timing: I have availability Thursday 2027-05-05 10:00-12:00 Pacific or Friday 2027-05-06 09:00-11:00. Please confirm preference.

Deliverables within 24 hours of the run: perf summary PDF (p50/p95, throughput), streaming TB metrics, CPU/GPU utilization graphs, and a short list of tuning recommendations.

- Rishi Malhotra | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: John Miller <john.miller@acmepay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO checklist & next steps - AcmePay

Rishi / Marissa - thanks, that plan looks good.

We can do Thursday 2027-05-05 10:00-11:00 PT. Priya has uploaded the sample payloads and a small CSV to the Drive folder (link above). We'll provide an ephemeral key for the run - please let me know if you need a specific scope or IP allowlist.

Decision criteria notes (so we're aligned):
- Must meet p95 <= 100ms (preferred 80ms) under a representative burst profile
- Streaming must support time-to-first-byte < 50ms in the stream-enabled path
- Token cost estimate for 1M requests (we need a ballpark to compare against internal budget)
- Output fidelity: no quantization artifacts that materially change generated output vs. baseline (we'll spot-check a few samples)

If we see major regressions on any of the above we'll escalate. Otherwise, if the run is a match we'll move to a short POC contract (term & pricing to be discussed).

- John
